json.summary: A young bearded man asks his grandmother if he can borrow his late grandfather Tibor's old oilcloth butterfly-collecting bag from the shed. The grandmother insists that the shed is not the chaotic mess it appears to be, but a brilliant system, and hands him a photo of Tibor to get him into the right mindset. Venturing off-panel into the shed, the grandson is horrified to discover impossible and terrifying contents: a helicopter turbine blocking a staircase, followed by the dried mummy of a Caucasian man. The grandmother nonchalantly clarifies that the corpse was the result of a property boundary dispute, and when the grandson discovers the victim's pickled organs and a heart in a jam jar, she simply praises her late husband's meticulous nature.

characters.name: grandmother in armchair
characters.description: An elderly woman with prominent glasses, a twin-horned hairstyle, and an unflappable, deadpan demeanor; speaks colloquially and calmly treats murder and bizarre hoarding as perfectly normal qualities of her late husband Tibor.

characters.name: bearded man
characters.description: A young man with a black beard, topknot-style hair, and a T-shirt; begins politely asking for old gear, but quickly devolves into loud, profanity-laced terror and disgust as he explores the shed.

panels.description: In a room, the grandmother sits comfortably in an armchair while the bearded man stands before her asking about grandpa Tibor's old oilcloth butterfly bag. The grandmother cheerfully tells him it must be out in the shed, eliciting an apprehensive sigh from him.

The grandmother holds up a framed portrait of grandpa Tibor, explaining to the man that the shed only looks like a bombed-out mess and that looking at the photo will help him understand Tibor's brilliant organizational logic.

The grandmother remains seated alone in her chair as the man speaks from off-panel inside the shed, asking in bewilderment if what he is seeing is a helicopter turbine, to which she casually confirms that the stairs start behind it.

A massive jagged scream bubble erupts from off-panel as the grandson shrieks in terror at finding a dried human mummy. The grandmother calmly responds with a single deadpan word explaining the corpse.
The grandmother smiles and raises a finger approvingly while the off-panel grandson shouts in revulsion about finding the mummy's organs in an aquarium and its heart in a jam jar.

notes: 'Sufni' (shed / lean-to workshop) is an iconic feature of rural and suburban Hungarian houses, notorious for being packed to the ceiling with decades of hoarded junk, tools, and bizarre scrap metal that the patriarch insisted was 'organized'.
'Kupleráj' literally means brothel/whorehouse, but colloquially refers to an utter disaster of a mess or chaotic room. 'Kibaszott kupleráj' translates to 'a fucking pigsty/disaster area'.

'Telekvita' (boundary line / land dispute) is a classic trope in rural and suburban Hungary, where neighbors obsessively feud for decades over fence placement, encroaching trees, or shared property lines. The dark comedy comes from the deadpan revelation that grandpa Tibor resolved a mundane land dispute by murdering and mummifying his neighbor.

'Lekváros üveg' (jam jar) evokes typical Hungarian domestic hoarding, where empty preserve jars are washed and reused endlessly to store screws, paint, fat, or—in Tibor's gruesome case—a victim's heart.
Profanity escalation: The grandson's speech devolves from polite inquiries into heavy swearing: 'Basszameg' (fuck it / holy shit), 'bazmeg' (fuck / for fuck's sake), and 'fújbazmeg' (yuck, fuck me).
Regions r10 and r11 combine into a single sentence: 'Tiborom precíz ember volt!' ('My Tibor was a meticulous man!'), spoken with pride by the grandmother.
